Declare an operating system and consumer-selected CPU set as one export platform.

Example: `godot_export_platform(name = "android", operating_system = "android",
cpus = ["@platforms//cpu:armv7", "@platforms//cpu:aarch64"])`.

Select the resulting label with --platforms. C++ compiler, debug symbol, signing and
variant settings stay independent of it. See the platform guide for engine and SDK setup.

<a id="godot_export_platform"></a>

## godot_export_platform

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot/platforms:defs.bzl", "godot_export_platform")

godot_export_platform(<a href="#godot_export_platform-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_export_platform-operating_system">operating_system</a>, <a href="#godot_export_platform-cpus">cpus</a>, <a href="#godot_export_platform-environment">environment</a>, <a href="#godot_export_platform-parents">parents</a>, <a href="#godot_export_platform-constraint_values">constraint_values</a>,
                      <a href="#godot_export_platform-exec_properties">exec_properties</a>, <a href="#godot_export_platform-visibility">visibility</a>)
</pre>

Create an export platform and, for mobile, its private platform slices.

A child platform, `platform(parents = [":android_arm64"])` for an export platform
named `android_arm64`, keeps the export platform's operating system, CPUs
and platform slices. The child's own constraints, flags and execution properties
apply only to application packaging and a desktop runtime: content export, the
project's extension libraries and mobile platform slices build for this export
platform or its platform slices, and a desktop export platform is its own platform
slice. Put properties those actions need on `parents`, `constraint_values` or
`exec_properties` here. A child that sets another operating system, CPU or iOS
environment fails analysis.

### Default outputs
- metadata (none): select operating system and CPUs; no run behavior


**PARAMETERS**


| Name  | Description | Default Value |
| :------------- | :------------- | :------------- |
| <a id="godot_export_platform-name"></a>name |  Public export platform target name, selected through --platforms.   |  none |
| <a id="godot_export_platform-operating_system"></a>operating_system |  Operating system: linux, macos, android or ios.   |  none |
| <a id="godot_export_platform-cpus"></a>cpus |  Nonempty unique list of `@platforms//cpu` constraint values Godot can express: `armv7`, `aarch64` (or its alias `arm64`), `x86_32`, `x86_64` and `riscv64`. Desktops take one CPU, an iOS device `aarch64` and the iOS Simulator `aarch64` or `x86_64`. Whether a CPU builds is decided by the registered runtime components: an application for a CPU without one fails analysis.   |  none |
| <a id="godot_export_platform-environment"></a>environment |  iOS device (default) or simulator; omit for other operating systems.   |  `None` |
| <a id="godot_export_platform-parents"></a>parents |  At most one parent platform for custom properties every platform slice shares. The export platform's operating system, CPU, environment and mobile CPU flags replace its own.   |  `[]` |
| <a id="godot_export_platform-constraint_values"></a>constraint_values |  Additional constraints shared by the export platform and its platform slices. Operating system, CPU and iOS environment constraints are owned by this macro.   |  `[]` |
| <a id="godot_export_platform-exec_properties"></a>exec_properties |  Execution properties shared by the export platform and every platform slice.   |  `{}` |
| <a id="godot_export_platform-visibility"></a>visibility |  Visibility of the public export platform; generated platform slices remain private.   |  `None` |
